request.prompt:
Job T03: usp_build_fact_premium_earned. Parameters per run, in order: AsOfDate=2025-12-31.

Code:
  1 | /*==============================================================================
  2 |   Job       dw.usp_build_fact_premium_earned
  3 |   Purpose   Premium fact for finance: one row per premium transaction, converted
  4 |             to EUR at the rate published on or before the booking date, with
  5 |             the premium earned as at the reporting date.
  6 |   Author    MOD
  7 |   Run by    FIN_MONTH_END, after dw.usp_load_dim_policy
  8 |   Output    dw.fact_premium_earned (full refresh)
  9 | 
 10 |   Change log
 11 |     2016-01-11  MOD  Initial version (CR-0904)
 12 |     2016-07-04  MOD  Sterling and dollar business converted to EUR (CR-0977)
 13 |     2018-03-19  PK   Policy surrogate key and line of business from dim_policy (CR-1290)
 14 |     2019-09-30  PK   Daily rate and monthly instalment for the cash-flow model (CR-1510)
 15 |     2021-02-15  MOD  First instalment due date for the direct debit file (CR-1618)
 16 |     2023-05-08  JMcK Earned percentage for the finance dashboard (INC-2301)
 17 | ==============================================================================*/
 18 | SET NOCOUNT ON;
 19 | GO
 20 | IF OBJECT_ID(N'dw.fact_premium_earned', N'U') IS NULL
 21 | CREATE TABLE dw.fact_premium_earned (
 22 |     txn_id                  INT            NOT NULL,
 23 |     policy_id               INT            NOT NULL,
 24 |     policy_sk               INT            NOT NULL,
 25 |     lob_code                VARCHAR(5)     NOT NULL,
 26 |     txn_type                VARCHAR(4)     NOT NULL,
 27 |     txn_date                DATE           NOT NULL,
 28 |     effective_from          DATE           NOT NULL,
 29 |     effective_to            DATE           NOT NULL,
 30 |     currency                CHAR(3)        NOT NULL,
 31 |     amount                  DECIMAL(12,2)  NOT NULL,
 32 |     fx_rate                 DECIMAL(18,8)  NOT NULL,
 33 |     written_eur             DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
 34 |     term_days               INT            NOT NULL,
 35 |     earned_days             INT            NOT NULL,
 36 |     earned_pct              DECIMAL(5,2)   NOT NULL,
 37 |     earned_eur              DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
 38 |     unearned_eur            DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
 39 |     daily_rate_eur          DECIMAL(12,4)  NOT NULL,
 40 |     monthly_instalment_eur  DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
 41 |     first_due_date          DATE           NOT NULL,
 42 |     as_of_date              DATE           NOT NULL,
 43 |     CONSTRAINT pk_dw_fact_premium_earned PRIMARY KEY (txn_id)
 44 | );
 45 | GO
 46 | CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dw.usp_build_fact_premium_earned
 47 |     @AsOfDate DATE
 48 | AS
 49 | BEGIN
 50 |     SET NOCOUNT ON;
 51 | 
 52 |     DECLARE @job_name  VARCHAR(128) = 'dw.usp_build_fact_premium_earned',
 53 |             @rows      INT,
 54 |             @err_msg   NVARCHAR(4000),
 55 |             @err_no    INT;
 56 | 
 57 |     BEGIN TRY
 58 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';
 59 | 
 60 |         /* Transactions with their EUR rate: EUR as is, other currencies at the
 61 |            latest rate on or before the booking date (later row wins on revisions) */
 62 |         IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#txn') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #txn;
 63 | 
 64 |         SELECT  t.txn_id, t.policy_id, UPPER(RTRIM(t.txn_type)) AS txn_type, t.txn_date,
 65 |                 t.effective_from, t.effective_to, t.currency, t.amount,
 66 |                 CAST(1 AS DECIMAL(18,8)) AS fx_rate
 67 |         INTO    #txn
 68 |         FROM    stg.premium_transactions t WITH (NOLOCK)
 69 |         WHERE   t.currency = 'EUR'
 70 |           AND   t.txn_date <= @AsOfDate;
 71 | 
 72 |         INSERT INTO #txn (txn_id, policy_id, txn_type, txn_date, effective_from, effective_to,
 73 |                           currency, amount, fx_rate)
 74 |         SELECT  t.txn_id, t.policy_id, UPPER(RTRIM(t.txn_type)), t.txn_date,
 75 |                 t.effective_from, t.effective_to, t.currency, t.amount, fx.rate_to_eur
 76 |         FROM    stg.premium_transactions t WITH (NOLOCK)
 77 |         CROSS APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 r.rate_to_eur
 78 |                      FROM   stg.fx_rates r WITH (NOLOCK)
 79 |                      WHERE  r.currency = t.currency
 80 |                        AND  r.rate_date <= t.txn_date
 81 |                      ORDER BY r.rate_date DESC, r._row_seq DESC) fx
 82 |         WHERE   t.currency <> 'EUR'
 83 |           AND   t.txn_date <= @AsOfDate;
 84 | 
 85 |         SELECT @rows = COUNT(*) FROM #txn;
 86 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'transactions', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
 87 | 
 88 |         /* Days of cover and days earned by the reporting date */
 89 |         IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#earn') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #earn;
 90 | 
 91 |         SELECT  x.*,
 92 |                 CAST(ROUND(x.amount * x.fx_rate, 2) AS DECIMAL(14,2)) AS written_eur,
 93 |                 DATEDIFF(DAY, x.effective_from, x.effective_to) + 1  AS term_days,
 94 |                 CASE WHEN @AsOfDate < x.effective_from THEN 0
 95 |                      WHEN @AsOfDate >= x.effective_to  THEN DATEDIFF(DAY, x.effective_from, x.effective_to) + 1
 96 |                      ELSE DATEDIFF(DAY, x.effective_from, @AsOfDate) + 1
 97 |                 END AS earned_days
 98 |         INTO    #earn
 99 |         FROM    #txn x;
100 | 
101 |         BEGIN TRANSACTION;
102 | 
103 |         TRUNCATE TABLE dw.fact_premium_earned;
104 | 
105 |         INSERT INTO dw.fact_premium_earned
106 |                (txn_id, policy_id, policy_sk, lob_code, txn_type, txn_date, effective_from,
107 |                 effective_to, currency, amount, fx_rate, written_eur, term_days, earned_days,
108 |                 earned_pct, earned_eur, unearned_eur, daily_rate_eur, monthly_instalment_eur,
109 |                 first_due_date, as_of_date)
110 |         SELECT  e.txn_id,
111 |                 e.policy_id,
112 |                 p.policy_sk,
113 |                 p.lob_code,
114 |                 e.txn_type,
115 |                 e.txn_date,
116 |                 e.effective_from,
117 |                 e.effective_to,
118 |                 e.currency,
119 |                 e.amount,
120 |                 e.fx_rate,
121 |                 e.written_eur,
122 |                 e.term_days,
123 |                 e.earned_days,
124 |                 e.earned_days * 100 / e.term_days,
125 |                 ROUND(e.written_eur * e.earned_days / 365, 2),
126 |                 e.written_eur - ROUND(e.written_eur * e.earned_days / 365, 2),
127 |                 ROUND(e.written_eur / e.term_days, 4, 1),
128 |                 ROUND(e.written_eur / ISNULL(NULLIF(e.term_days / 30, 0), 1), 2),
129 |                 DATEADD(MONTH, 1, EOMONTH(e.effective_from)),
130 |                 @AsOfDate
131 |         FROM    #earn e
132 |         JOIN    dw.dim_policy p WITH (NOLOCK)
133 |                 ON p.policy_id = e.policy_id
134 |                AND p.is_current = 'Y';
135 | 
136 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
137 | 
138 |         COMMIT TRANSACTION;
139 | 
140 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'dw.fact_premium_earned', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
141 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
142 |     END TRY
143 |     BEGIN CATCH
144 |         IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
145 | 
146 |         SELECT  @err_msg = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
147 |                 @err_no  = ERROR_NUMBER();
148 | 
149 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
150 |              @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
151 |         THROW;
152 |     END CATCH
153 | END;
154 | GO

Input tables:
- stg.premium_transactions: txn_id INT NOT NULL, policy_id INT NOT NULL, txn_type VARCHAR(4) NOT NULL, txn_date DATE NOT NULL, effective_from DATE NOT NULL, effective_to DATE NOT NULL, amount DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL, currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL
- stg.fx_rates: rate_date DATE NOT NULL, currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL, rate_to_eur DECIMAL(18,8) NOT NULL, source VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL
- dw.dim_policy: policy_sk INT NOT NULL, policy_id INT NOT NULL, policy_number VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, customer_id INT NOT NULL, customer_segment CHAR(4), product_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, product_name NVARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, lob_code VARCHAR(5) NOT NULL, broker_code VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL, broker_name NVARCHAR(80), status VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL, inception_date DATE NOT NULL, expiry_date DATE NOT NULL, cancellation_date DATE, annual_premium DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL, currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL, vehicle_reg VARCHAR(12), ncd_years INT, valid_from DATE NOT NULL, valid_to DATE NOT NULL, is_current CHAR(1) NOT NULL, source_snapshot_date DATE NOT NULL, load_ts DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL

Semantic traps to test (one case per distinct trap id):
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 69-69: currency is CHAR(3) text. Under a CI collation, 'eur' or 'Eur' also matches 'EUR', but Spark's binary compare would drop those rows from the EUR branch.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 69-69: currency is CHAR(3), and SQL Server ignores trailing spaces in the comparison. A value like 'EU ' or a padded source value would compare differently in Spark.
- TSQL-08 (TOP and TOP WITH TIES) at lines 77-81: TOP 1 is ordered by rate_date DESC, _row_seq DESC. If _row_seq ties within a date, the row chosen is arbitrary, so the window ordering must match.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 79-79: The rate lookup joins on the CHAR(3) currency columns. The CI collation matches case variants such as 'usd' to 'USD', and Spark's join would miss them.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 79-79: The CHAR(3) join on currency ignores trailing spaces in the legacy engine. Spark needs trimmed keys to match the same way.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 82-82: The <> 'EUR' test is case-insensitive in the legacy engine. In Spark, lower-case 'eur' rows would go to the FX branch and also be missing from the EUR branch.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 82-82: currency is CHAR(3) and the legacy comparison ignores trailing spaces. Spark compares the exact string.
- TSQL-07 (DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values) at lines 92-92: DECIMAL(12,2)*DECIMAL(18,8) is rounded half away from zero to 2 places and cast to DECIMAL(14,2). Spark must keep decimal types and HALF_UP rounding, not doubles.
- TSQL-03 (Integer division truncates) at lines 124-124: earned_days*100/term_days is INT/INT, so the percentage is truncated to a whole number before it is stored in DECIMAL(5,2) (e.g. 33.00, not 33.33). Spark's / would return a fraction.
- TSQL-07 (DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values) at lines 125-125: Decimal * int / 365 follows SQL Server's precision and scale rules for division, then ROUND to 2 places half away from zero. Spark's decimal division and rounding must reproduce this.
- TSQL-07 (DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values) at lines 126-126: Unearned is written_eur minus the separately rounded earned amount, so the decimal scale and rounding of the subtrahend must match the legacy result.
- TSQL-07 (DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values) at lines 127-127: ROUND(x, 4, 1) truncates rather than rounds. Spark needs an explicit truncation of the decimal quotient (e.g. floor-based for positive values, toward zero for negatives), not F.round.
- TSQL-03 (Integer division truncates) at lines 128-128: term_days/30 is integer division, so the instalment count is truncated: 365 days gives 12, and under 30 days gives 0, which falls back to 1.
- TSQL-07 (DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values) at lines 128-128: Decimal divided by an int count, then ROUND to 2 places half away from zero into DECIMAL(14,2). The decimal types must be kept.
- TSQL-18 (EOMONTH and DATEADD at month-end) at lines 129-129: DATEADD(MONTH,1,EOMONTH(d)) clamps without snapping to month-end: an end of February gives the 28th/29th of March. Spark's add_months on a last-day input returns the 31st, so the result would differ.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 134-134: is_current is CHAR(1) text. Under the CI collation a lower-case 'y' also matches, and Spark's exact compare would drop those policies from the inner join.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 134-134: is_current is CHAR(1). The trailing-space-insensitive compare is a latent risk only if values are stored with spaces.
request.system_prompt:
You are the test author agent of LANSH, a factory that migrates legacy T-SQL (SQL Server 2022) jobs to PySpark and must reproduce their output exactly. For each semantic trap you are given, write one small input set (5 to 20 rows per table) on which a naive translation of this job would give a different result from the legacy engine, while the job still produces output rows.

- Use only the job's input tables and their columns; respect each column's legacy type and length (a VARCHAR(5) value has at most 5 characters) and fill every NOT NULL column.
- Write every value as text: dates YYYY-MM-DD, datetimes YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, numbers as plain decimals; use null for NULL. Leave _row_seq out: the rows' order is their _row_seq.
- Include the related rows the job needs to produce output (for example, a claim's payments) and rows on both sides of the trap (the variant that a naive translation mishandles, and the canonical value).
- The expected output is computed by running the legacy job itself on your rows, so never state expected values.

cases.description: Currency case variants: 'eur' and 'Eur' rows belong to the EUR branch (lines 69/82). Under the CI collation they get rate 1, and they must not go to the FX branch. A naive binary compare would drop them, or send them looking for a rate. The FX join on line 79 must match txn 'usd' to fx 'USD', and txn 'GBP' to fx 'Gbp'. In dim_policy, policy 104 has is_current 'y' (line 134), so its rows join only under the CI compare. Canonical 'EUR'/'USD'/'Y' rows are included as controls, along with a non-current 'N' row.

Trailing spaces in CHAR(3) currency keys (lines 69/79/82). Txn currency 'CH' matches fx 'CH ', and txn 'JP ' matches fx 'JP'. The legacy engine pads both and ignores trailing spaces, so the rows find their rates. A naive exact-string join drops them. txn_type values carry trailing spaces ('NB  ', 'MTA '), and RTRIM removes them. Canonical 'EUR' and 'USD' rows are included as controls, and is_current is 'Y'.

FX TOP 1 tie-break (lines 77-81). USD has two rates on 2025-06-01 (0.92 at seq 2, a revision 0.93 at seq 4). GBP has two rates on 2025-06-01 (1.18 at seq 5, 1.17 at seq 6). The legacy engine picks the later _row_seq. A window ordered only by rate_date, or by insertion order, could pick the other row. A USD rate dated after some txn dates (2025-07-01, inserted first) must be ignored for those txns and used for a later txn. A txn on 2025-05-15 must take the older 0.91 rate. A EUR row is included as a control.

Decimal rounding, lines 92 and 125-128. Several amount*rate products land exactly on half a cent: 10.01*0.5=5.005, 2.35*1.5=3.525, -10.01*0.5=-5.005. Rounding half away from zero is required. Doubles or HALF_EVEN would differ. CHF 999.99*1.07123457 tests the full-precision product. Partial-term EUR rows (1000.00 over 184 of 365 days, 333.33 over a short term) test the /365 decimal scale and unearned = written - ROUND(...). A negative EUR -100.00 over 365 days tests ROUND(x,4,1) truncation toward zero for the daily rate (floor would differ). Other rows give non-terminating quotients for the daily rate and the instalment.

Integer division, lines 124 and 128. A 3-day term with 1 earned day gives an earned_pct of 1*100/3, truncated to 33 (not 33.33). A 90-day term with 31 days earned gives 34, not 34.44. A 151-day term with 31 days earned gives 20 (3100/151=20.53, so rounding would give 21). A future-dated term earns 0. A fully earned 365-day term is included as a control. Instalments: a 365-day term gives a count of 12 (not 12.17). A 20-day term gives 0, which falls back to 1. A 59-day term gives 1 and a 366-day term gives 12. All rows are EUR.

first_due_date = DATEADD(MONTH,1,EOMONTH(effective_from)), line 129. These effective_from dates have month-ends shorter than the following month: Feb 2025 (to Mar 28), Feb 2024 leap (to Mar 29), Apr 30 (to May 30), Jun 30 (to Jul 30), Sep (to Oct 30), Nov 30 (to Dec 30). The legacy engine does not snap to month-end, but a last-day-preserving add_months would return the 31st. Controls: January (clamps to Feb 28), Mar 31 (to Apr 30) and Dec 2025 (to Jan 31, 2026). All rows are EUR.
